diff --git a/solution/.gitignore b/solution/.gitignorenew file mode 100644index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..b14495a20ac45e23628cefb8467262f517ff66bf--- /dev/null+++ b/solution/.gitignore@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@+__pycache__/+*.pyc+*.log+profiler/diff --git a/solution/README.md b/solution/README.mdnew file mode 100644index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..0c9e1b51966a20181b2ba5da16c6560c7ac10c75--- /dev/null+++ b/solution/README.md@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@+# Qwen3 on one Ascend 910B++This delivery implements an OpenAI-compatible Qwen3 server using Python,+PyTorch, and the base runtime's `torch_npu` / CANN operators. It loads the+supplied safetensors shards in bfloat16 onto the visible NPU. It does not+download models or dependencies.++`bootstrap.sh` checks the offline installation without modifying the base+Python environment. `launch.sh` replaces itself with the foreground server.+Both entrypoints use the `OPENBUILD_*` environment defined by the delivery+contract. Tokenizers, safetensors, Jinja2, and MarkupSafe are vendored, together+with their distribution metadata and licenses. Python, PyTorch, torch_npu,+and their runtime dependencies come from the declared base runtime.++## Execution++* A single worker owns the NPU and continuously batches up to 64 requests.+  HTTP handlers enqueue work and consume generated tokens independently.+* Prefill packs variable-length prompts, applies causal attention with their+  actual sequence boundaries, and writes a paged KV cache. The scheduler+  admits up to 4096 prompt tokens per iteration, then advances active decodes.+* Each transformer layer uses fused QKV and gate/up matrix multiplications,+  RMS normalization, rotary embedding, SwiGLU, and CANN inference attention.+  The vocabulary projection and greedy argmax also execute on the NPU.+* Decode graphs cover batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Actual sequence+  lengths are updated on a separate stream. External events hold each+  attention task until its current parameters are ready, overlapping host+  updates with NPU execution. Padding uses a reserved cache block, separate+  from all live requests.+  Host metadata uses array views of pinned input buffers to avoid dispatching+  hundreds of scalar tensor writes for each large batch.+* With one active request, a bounded history of this launch's generated+  tokens can propose up to four continuations. Fresh Qwen forward passes+  verify them on the NPU, using incremental causal attention at every+  position. Only tokens that match Qwen's greedy selection are accepted;+  the first mismatch uses Qwen's replacement. Future unaccepted KV positions+  are excluded from attention and overwritten. Measured acceptance and cost+  select ordinary decoding when verification is slower. Larger batches use+  ordinary decoding and skip proposal maintenance.+* Recurring prefill shapes can also use captured graphs. Their token IDs,+  positions, and cache destinations are fresh inputs; graphs do not cache+  responses or prompt prefixes. Uncaptured shapes execute eagerly.+* The cache contains 1408 blocks of 128 tokens. Blocks are reserved for each+  request's full context and reclaimed on completion or cancellation. When+  capacity is exhausted, new requests wait in the admission queue.++The supplied tokenizer JSON and Jinja chat template define the prompt exactly.+Incremental byte-level detokenization preserves Unicode and whitespace. Usage+counts the actual prompt IDs and generated IDs, including a sampled EOS token.+`ignore_eos` continues model execution through EOS to the requested length.+Streaming responses include a finish record, requested usage, and `[DONE]`.++SIGTERM and SIGINT stop admission and the scheduling loop. The HTTP listener+closes, queued handlers receive a shutdown event, and the NPU worker is joined.+The service creates no child processes or detached services. Runtime caches+belong to `OPENBUILD_ENV_DIR`; the model projection remains read-only.++## Development checks++The authoritative commands are provided by the task:++```sh+TASK_MODE=describe bash "$TASK_DIR/run/describe.sh"+TASK_MODE=dry_run bash "$TASK_DIR/run/smoke.sh"+bash "$TASK_DIR/run/correctness.sh"+bash "$TASK_DIR/run/development_correctness.sh"+bash "$TASK_DIR/run/benchmark_once.sh"+bash "$TASK_DIR/run/cleanup.sh"+```++`tests/http_contract.py` replays a supplied cases file against a running+server and compares isolated, streaming, and mixed concurrent generation.+It also checks natural EOS, fixed-length decoding, and invalid requests.+`tests/bench_model.py` measures real model prefill and decode execution on the+NPU, independently of the authoritative HTTP benchmark. Diagnostic timing+output is printed to stdout and is not a benchmark result.+`tests/bench_speculation.py` compares every generated token against ordinary+decoding with serial graph updates, using a supplied JSONL request dataset.++For diagnostics, `QWEN_USE_GRAPHS=0` selects eager execution, and+`QWEN_PREFILL_GRAPHS=0` disables only prefill capture. `QWEN_KV_BLOCKS`,+`QWEN_MAX_BATCH` (at most 64), and `QWEN_PREFILL_TOKENS` control resource limits.+`QWEN_SPECULATE=0` disables token proposals; `QWEN_OVERLAP_UPDATES=0` serializes+graph updates and replay for comparison.+The default settings require about 40 GiB for model weights and KV storage,+plus graph and temporary buffers. Host graph updates originally contributed+about 6 ms per decode step; overlapping them removes most of that idle time.+The remaining steady-state cost is reading model weights and KV tensors and+executing the matrix multiplications.diff --git a/solution/bootstrap.sh b/solution/bootstrap.shnew file mode 100755index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..f1ca709cd724f4dfb5c65e0de465ba658508dc8c--- /dev/null+++ b/solution/bootstrap.sh@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@+#!/usr/bin/env bash+set -euo pipefail+: "${OPENBUILD_SOLUTION_DIR:?}" "${OPENBUILD_ENV_DIR:?}"+mkdir -p "${OPENBUILD_ENV_DIR}"+export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1+export PYTHONPATH="${OPENBUILD_SOLUTION_DIR}/vendor:${OPENBUILD_SOLUTION_DIR}${PYTHONPATH:+:${PYTHONPATH}}"+python3 - <<'PY'+import importlib, os+from pathlib import Path+for name in ('torch', 'torch_npu', 'tokenizers', 'safetensors', 'jinja2'):+    importlib.import_module(name)+for name in ('OPENBUILD_MODEL_PATH', 'OPENBUILD_TOKENIZER_PATH'):+    if not Path(os.environ[name]).is_dir():+        raise RuntimeError(f'{name} must be a read-only model directory')+print('Offline dependencies ready; base environment unchanged.', flush=True)+PYdiff --git a/solution/draft.py b/solution/draft.pynew file mode 100644index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..65c181c848c5ab4f30cf38d1e22972a83c4af9af--- /dev/null+++ b/solution/draft.py@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@+"""Bounded, in-memory token proposals from this launch's model generations.++A proposal is never a response. Every proposed token must be checked by a+fresh target-model forward pass before it can be returned to a client.+"""+from collections import OrderedDict+++class DraftCache:+    def __init__(self, capacity=65536, max_ngram=8, min_ngram=3, lookahead=4):+        self.capacity = capacity+        self.max_ngram = max_ngram+        self.min_ngram = min_ngram+        self.lookahead = lookahead+        self.entries = OrderedDict()++    def observe(self, sequence):+        """Record one newly generated token, retaining its real continuation."""+        end = len(sequence) - 1+        for size in range(self.min_ngram, min(self.max_ngram, end) + 1):+            key = tuple(sequence[end - size:end])+            old = self.entries.get(key, ())+            # Keep one older occurrence with a longer available continuation.+            previous = next((ref for ref in old if len(ref[0]) - ref[1] >= self.lookahead), None)+            current = (sequence, end)+            self.entries[key] = (current, previous) if previous is not None else (current,)+            self.entries.move_to_end(key)+            while len(self.entries) > self.capacity:+                self.entries.popitem(last=False)++    def propose(self, prefix):+        proposal = []+        context = list(prefix[-self.max_ngram:])+        while len(proposal) < self.lookahead:+            following = self._lookup(context)+            if not following:+                break+            following = following[:self.lookahead - len(proposal)]+            proposal.extend(following)+            context.extend(following)+        return proposal++    def _lookup(self, prefix):+        for size in range(min(len(prefix), self.max_ngram), self.min_ngram - 1, -1):+            refs = self.entries.get(tuple(prefix[-size:]))+            if refs:+                refs = sorted(refs, key=lambda ref: min(self.lookahead, len(ref[0]) - ref[1]), reverse=True)+                for sequence, start in refs:+                    proposal = sequence[start:start + self.lookahead]+                    if proposal:+                        return proposal+        return []diff --git started+        if warm:+            old = self.normal_cost.get(batch, elapsed)+            self.normal_cost[batch] = 0.8 * old + 0.2 * elapsed+        return [[token] for token in tokens]++    def verify(self, requests, proposals, steps):+        m = self.model+        count = len(requests)+        batch = next(b for b in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) if b >= count)+        if (batch, steps) not in self.graphs:+            self.create_graph(batch, steps)+        started = time.perf_counter()+        graph, meta, table, output, cpu_meta, cpu_table = self.graphs[batch, steps]+        token_ids, positions, slots = [], [], []+        lengths = [steps] * batch+        cpu_table.zero_()+        for i, (req, proposal) in enumerate(zip(requests, proposals)):+            pos = len(req.prompt) + len(req.output) - align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pallets/markupsafe/refs/heads/stable/docs/_static/markupsafe-name.svg" alt="" height="150"></div>++# MarkupSafe++MarkupSafe implements a text object that escapes characters so it is+safe to use in HTML and XML. Characters that have special meanings are+replaced so that they display as the actual characters. This mitigates+injection attacks, meaning untrusted user input can safely be displayed+on a page.+++## Examples++```pycon+>>> from markupsafe import Markup, escape++>>> # escape replaces special characters and wraps in Markup+>>> escape("<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>")+Markup('&lt;script&gt;alert(document.cookie);&lt;/script&gt;')++>>> # wrap in Markup to mark text "safe" and prevent escaping+>>> Markup("<strong>Hello</strong>")+Markup('<strong>hello</strong>')++>>> escape(Markup("<strong>Hello</strong>"))+Markup('<strong>hello</strong>')++>>> # Markup is a str subclass+>>> # methods and operators escape their arguments+>>> template = Markup("Hello <em>{name}</em>")+>>> template.format(name='"World"')+Markup('Hello <em>&#34;World&#34;</em>')+```++## Donate++The Pallets organization develops and supports MarkupSafe and other+popular packages. extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: pytest-asyncio ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: requests ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: numpy ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: datasets ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: ruff ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: ty ; extra == 'testing'+Requires-Dist: sphinx ; extra == 'docs'+Requires-Dist: sphinx-rtd-theme ; extra == 'docs'+Requires-Dist: setuptools-rust ; extra == 'docs'+Requires-Dist: tokenizers[testing] ; extra == 'dev'+Provides-Extra: testing+Provides-Extra: docs+Provides-Extra: dev+Keywords: NLP,tokenizer,BPE,transformer,deep learning+Author-email: Nicolas Patry <redacted@example.invalid>, Anthony Moi <redacted@example.invalid>+Requires-Python: >=3.9+Description-Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=UTF-8; variant=GFM+Project-URL: Homepage, https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers+Project-URL: Source, https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers++<p align="center">+    <br>+    <img src="https://huggingface.co/landing/assets/tokenizers/tokenizers-logo.png" width="600"/>+    <br>+<p>+<p align="center">+    <a href="https://badge.fury.io/py/tokenizers">+         <img alt="Build" src="https://badge.fury.io/py/tokenizers.svg">+    </a>+    <a href="https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/blob/master/LICENSE">+        <img alt="GitHub" src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/huggingface/tokenizers.svg?color=blue">+    </a>+</p>+<br>++# Tokenizers++Provides an implementation of today's most used tokenizers, with a focus on performance and+versatility.++Bindings over the [Rust](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/tree/master/tokenizers) implementation.+If you are interested in the High-level design, you can go check it there.++Otherwise, let's dive in!++## Main features:++ - Train new vocabularies and tokenize using 4 pre-made tokenizers (Bert WordPiece and the 3+   most common BPE versions).+ - Extremely fast (both training and tokenization), thanks to the Rust implementation. Takes+   less than 20 seconds to tokenize a GB of text on a server's CPU.+ - Easy to use, but also extremely versatile.+ - Designed for research and production.+ - Normalization comes with alignments tracking. It's always possible to get the part of the+   original sentence that corresponds to a given token.+ - Does all the pre-processing: Truncate, Pad, add the special tokens your model needs.++### Installation++#### With pip:++```bash+pip install tokenizers+```++#### From sources:++To use this method, you need to have the Rust installed:++```bash+# Install with:+curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh -s -- -y+export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"+```++Once Rust is installed, you can compile doing the following++```bash+git clone https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers+cd tokenizers/bindings/python++# Create a virtual env (you can use yours as well)+python -m venv .env+source .env/bin/activate++# Install `tokenizers` in the current virtual env+pip install -e .+```++### Load a pretrained tokenizer from the Hub++```python+from tokenizers import Tokenizer++tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-cased")+```++### Using the provided Tokenizers++We provide some pre-build tokenizers to cover the most common cases. You can easily load one of+these using some `vocab.json` and `merges.txt` files:++```python+from tokenizers import CharBPETokenizer++# Initialize a tokenizer+vocab = "./path/to/vocab.json"+merges = "./path/to/merges.txt"+tokenizer = CharBPETokenizer(vocab, merges)++# And then encode:+encoded = tokenizer.encode("I can feel the magic, can you?")+print(encoded.ids)+print(encoded.tokens)+```++And you can train them just as simply:++```python+from tokenizers import CharBPETokenizer++# Initialize a tokenizer+tokenizer = CharBPETokenizer()++# Then train it!+tokenizer.train([ "./path/to/files/1.txt", "./path/to/files/2.txt" ])++# Now, let's use it:+encoded = tokenizer.encode("I can feel the magic, can you?")++# And finally save it somewhere+tokenizer.save("./path/to/directory/my-bpe.tokenizer.json")+```++#### Provided Tokenizers++ - `CharBPETokenizer`: The original BPE+ - `ByteLevelBPETokenizer`: The byte level version of the BPE+ - `SentencePieceBPETokenizer`: A BPE implementation compatible with the one used by SentencePiece+ - `BertWordPieceTokenizer`: The famous Bert tokenizer, using WordPiece++All of these can be used and trained as explained above!++### Build your own++Whenever these provided tokenizers don't give you enough freedom, you can build your own tokenizer,+by putting all the different parts you need together.+You can check how we implemented the [provided tokenizers](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/tree/master/bindings/python/py_src/tokenizers/implementations) and adapt them easily to your own needs.++#### Building a byte-level BPE++Here is an example showing how to build your own byte-level BPE by putting all the different pieces+together, and then saving it to a single file:++```python+from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, pre_tokenizers, decoders, trainers, processors++# Initialize a tokenizer+tokenizer = Tokenizer(models.BPE())++# Customize pre-tokenization and decoding+tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.ByteLevel(add_prefix_space=True)+tokenizer.decoder = decoders.ByteLevel()+tokenizer.post_processor = processors.ByteLevel(trim_offsets=True)++# And then train+trainer = trainers.BpeTrainer(+    vocab_size=20000,+    min_frequency=2,+    initial_alphabet=pre_tokenizers.ByteLevel.alphabet()+)+tokenizer.train([+    "./path/to/dataset/1.txt",+    "./path/to/dataset/2.txt",+    "./path/to/dataset/3.txt"+], trainer=trainer)++# And Save it+tokenizer.save("byte-level-bpe.tokenizer.json", pretty=True)+```++Now, when you want to use this tokenizer, this is as simple as:++```python+from tokenizers import Tokenizer++tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file("byte-level-bpe.tokenizer.json")++encoded = tokenizer.encode("I can feel the magic, can you?")+```++### Typing support and `stub.py`++The compiled PyO3 extension does not expose type annotations, so editors and type checkers would otherwise see most objects as `Any`. The `stub.py` helper walks the loaded extension modules, renders `.pyi` stub files (plus minimal forwarding `__init__.py` shims), and formats them so that tools like mypy/pyright can understand the public API. Run `python stub.py` whenever you change the Python-visible surface to keep the generated stubs in sync.+diff --git a/solution/vendor/tokenizers-0.22.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE b/solution/vendor/tokenizers-0.22.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSEnew file mode 100644index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..261eeb9e9f8b2b4b0d119366dda99c6fd7d35c64--- /dev/null+++ b/solution/vendor/tokenizers-0.22.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@+                                 Apache License+                           Version 2.0, January 2004+                        http://www.apache.org/licenses/++   TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR USE, REPRODUCTION, AND DISTRIBUTION++   1.
